text: The man who crossed the finish line first at the nineteen-oh-four Olympic marathon had spent about eleven miles of it in a car.
Saint Louis, August nineteen-oh-four. Over thirty degrees, dusty dirt roads, and just one water station on the whole course.
Fred Lorz drops out after nine miles, and hops in a car. When it breaks down, he jogs to the finish, and the crowd cheers the winner.
He's caught. He says it was a joke.
The real leader, Thomas Hicks, is kept going by his trainers with egg whites, brandy, and strychnine. A terrible nineteen-oh-four idea.
Meanwhile, Cuban mail carrier Andarin Carvajal hasn't eaten in about forty hours, so he grabs apples from an orchard.
Bad apples. Cramps. He lies down for a nap.
Hicks crosses the line half carried and hallucinating, in about three and a half hours. Only fourteen runners finish.
Carvajal, after his nap, still comes fourth.
Luckily, Hicks got his gold. Unluckily, the man who took a car won the Boston Marathon the next year. On foot.
